cards.front: Recall a key point about Baroque Music 1650-1750
cards.back: Baroque music features basso continuo (keyboard + cello/bass providing harmonic foundation) and terraced dynamics (sudden dynamic shifts, not gradual).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Baroque Music 1650-1750
cards.back: Handel's Coronation Anthems exemplify Baroque grandeur: choral polyphony, orchestral doubling, majestic key choices and ceremonial character.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Baroque Music 1650-1750
cards.back: Ground bass (repeated bass pattern) provides structural foundation — used in arias and instrumental works by Purcell and Handel.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Baroque Music 1650-1750
cards.back: Ornamentation (trills, mordents, grace notes) was often improvised by performers — Baroque notation is simpler than what was actually played.

cards.front: What should you know about music exam tips?
cards.back: Identify Baroque features by NAME (basso continuo, terraced dynamics, ground bass). Reference Handel SPECIFICALLY. Explain how Baroque conventions create character.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Baroque music is just old classical music with no dynamics. Correct: Baroque music has TERRACED dynamics (sudden contrasts between loud and soft) as a deliberate style — gradual crescendos/diminuendos came later.
